To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the best NERC system for DEREKO is the Stanford NERC system, that the best model for this system is a CRF model trained on the entire training data and that the best NER classifier is the CRF model trained only on the most frequent entities.
the NERC system CRF+LSTM+CNN+ELMO+LSTM+LSTM+CRF+ELMO (see Table 3) is the most suitable NERC system for DEREKO.

(i) a system based on the CRFsuite implementation of Conditional Random Fields (CRFs) (Okazaki, 2007) outperforms the other two systems, and (ii) a model based on the Mallet implementation of Maximum Entropy (ME) classifiers (McCallum, 2002) outperforms all other models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two major questions: (i) How can we evaluate NERC systems when the evaluation data is a random sample of an unbalanced corpus? (ii) What is the optimal model for named-entity tagging DEREKO?
the following questions: 1) Which NERC system is optimal for DEREKO and which model is optimal for each system?
the following questions: 1. How can the performance of different NERC systems be compared when evaluated on a very large and unbalanced corpus of contemporary German?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best NERC system is not necessarily the best NERC model for the given corpus.
the best system and the best model for named entity recognition and tagging DEREKO is CRF++ (Chiang, 2007) with the default settings and the default model.
, for our data, the NERC system based on the Conditional Random Field (CRF) model is the most robust one and the most suitable for the DEREKO data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to train and evaluate NERC systems for DEREKO.
the system of the best-performing NERC system on the sample data is the one that performs best on the full DEREKO corpus.
, for our specific NERC task, we find that a combination of the CRF++ system with the C4.5 model yields the highest performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the best performing NERC system is not necessarily the best choice for a specific task, and that it is not possible to make a general statement about the performance of a NERC system on a specific task based on the performance of the NERC system on other tasks.
a NERC system trained on the full DEREKO corpus performs significantly better than any of its counterparts trained on the evaluation data.
, for a very large unbalanced corpus, a representative evaluation sample must be created and used in order to make reliable decisions about an optimal system and model.
